newsitem.title: CHINA: China futures must concentrate on major products.
newsitem.headline: China futures must concentrate on major products.

text.p: China's futures markets must further standardise operations to survive and concentrate on major products which are less subject to speculation, the official China Securities newspaper said on Monday.

The newspaper said a meeting of futures market experts held last week in Beijing concluded that China needed the futures markets and that trading in products such as copper, soybeans and green beans had been comparatively successful.
But they said over-speculation, particularly in small-volume products, had badly damaged the futures industry in recent years.
"The futures markets should work to recover their reputation this year," the newspaper said. "Regularisation (of trading) is their lifeline, and major products should be their soul."
The newspaper said it may be possible in 1997 to re-open such major futures contracts as long-grained rice, which would help increase trading volume.
"The problems that have appeared in the past with the futures markets are a management issue rather than one of the markets themselves," it said.
China's securities authorities sharply tightened controls on the futures exchanges in 1996 to curb speculation in a variety of futures contracts, including plywood, red beans and green beans.
Official references to the futures markets still indicate a high degree of suspicion about their activities.
The authorities have stressed that regularising trading rather than expansion should be the focus of the exchanges for the foreseeable future.
